Subject: Supplier transition notice — downstream subcontracting & governance checklist

Markus —

I wanted to give you early notice that Proxima will be transitioning a portion of our data processing (log aggregation and short-term metrics) to a partner, Nimbus Analytics, effective Aug 1. This is a standard supplier change but since it touches telemetry and PII-derived metadata used for routing we want to make sure your team has everything you need from us to update governance and the DPA.

Attached: Proxima_Supplier_Transition_Notice.pdf, Proxima_Subprocessor_Roster.xlsx

Can you confirm:
- Whether this requires an execution-level amendment to the MSA/order form or can be handled via a subcontractor addendum?
- Any evidence we should include up front (SOC 2, encryption-in-transit screenshots, access roster, subprocessor contract excerpt)?
- Preferred sign-off path and lead contact at Redwood?

We aim to keep this transition low-friction. If you prefer a quick call, I can make time tomorrow.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Legal Ops | Proxima Systems
[Attachment: Proxima_Supplier_Transition_Notice.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: Proxima_Subprocessor_Roster.xlsx (XLSX)]

Alicia —

Appreciate the heads-up and the attachments. Short answers up front:
- Likely a subcontractor notification plus a short DPA exhibit addendum; we usually only require an MSA amendment when there is a change in subprocessor that affects data residency or retention.
- Please include SOC 2 Type II report (recent), the redacted Nimbus subprocessor contract (key security clauses), and a brief description of data flows showing what telemetry fields will be routed. An access roster for Nimbus engineers with roles is helpful.
- I'll own the coordination on the Redwood side — copying legal for formal review.

I attached our initial redline-comments PDF (RI_redline_MSA_v1_comments.pdf) with a couple of items flagged for legal: audit access, incident notification SLA, and a short clause about transient KV cache retention for telemetry. Can you get the Nimbus contract excerpt by EOD tomorrow?

If it helps, let's do a 30-min sync. I'm free 1:30–3:00p PT tomorrow.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RI_redline_MSA_v1_comments.pdf (PDF)]

Team —

Reviewed Proxima's notice and Markus' comments. High level legal position and asks:
1) Evidence package required before approval: SOC 2 Type II (latest), Nimbus subprocessor agreement with the security & audit sections intact, independent pen test summary (or attest), and confirmation of encryption in transit and at rest for any PII-derived telemetry.
2) Redline points to add to DPA exhibit:
   - Explicit data scope for telemetry fields (define allowed processing).
   - Right to audit Nimbus, with 30 days notice and limits on sampling frequency.
   - Data deletion and verification procedures within 30 days of termination of the engagement.
   - Incident notification: 4 hour initial notification for suspected exfiltration, 24 hour substantive report requirement.
3) If Nimbus will perform any ML model training on derived features, we must treat that as a material change and require an MSA amendment.
4) Contractual fallback: if evidence is incomplete, require a temporary access restriction (no persistent copies) until remediation.

I'll prepare a short exhibit template we can attach to the existing DPA and propose edits to the order form's security appendix. Lauren — please confirm whether restrictions in (2) are operationally feasible. Evelyn — confirm retention/caching impacts.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

[Inline: excerpt from RI_redline_MSA_v1_comments.pdf highlighting sections 2.1, 6.3]

Alicia —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per legal & ops review, here's the agreed next steps:
1) Proxima to provide full evidence package (SOC2 Type II, signed Nimbus subprocessor excerpt, pen-test summary, and access roster) by EOD Wednesday (7/24).
2) Redwood will prepare a DPA exhibit addendum (initial draft attached) that captures: allowed telemetry fields, audit rights, incident SLA, and deletion verification. We will not require an MSA amendment unless Nimbus will retain persistent copies or train models.
3) If evidence is complete, we will execute via DocuSign and apply a 30-day post-execution monitoring window for the first month. If any red flags, we will apply temporary access limits until remediated.

I attached the initial DPA exhibit draft for your legalOps team to review. If you can get the Nimbus contract excerpt by tomorrow that keeps us on the timeline.

Happy to take the 30-min sync if you prefer — suggested 2pm PT Tues (7/23).

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
